RX STUDIO · POWERED BY MEDISELLER

How Rx Studio works

A walkthrough of the real app, recorded from a fresh start: setup, issuing a prescription, the PDF it makes, and how to run it on your laptop. Every screenshot below comes from dist/rx-studio.html, the same single file you'll open.

Run it on your laptop

No installation and no server. Pick one:

Easiest

Double-click the file

  1. Download dist/rx-studio.html from the GitHub branch claude/prescription-generation-tool-t1vnm4.
  2. Double-click it to open it in Chrome or Edge.
  3. Sign in: admin / Mediseller@123.

Works fully offline: everything it needs is inside the file.

Optional

Run it on localhost

  1. Open a terminal in the project folder.
  2. python3 -m http.server 8080
  3. Open http://localhost:8080/dist/rx-studio.html

The same app, served from a URL. Useful for testing on a phone over the same Wi-Fi (use the laptop's IP instead of localhost).

Good to know

Where things are kept

  • Setup (templates, field positions, doctors, medicines, settings, login) stays in that browser on that laptop.
  • No patient data is saved: each prescription exists only until you download or share it.
  • Move setup to another laptop with Settings → Export setup backup.

Start

Open the file and sign in.

One-time setup

Done once per company: about 10 minutes. Everything here is remembered in that browser.

Daily use: issuing a prescription

What a doctor or operator does after each teleconsultation: about 1 minute per patient.

On a phone

The same file adapts to phones.

The output

The PDF downloaded in step 15, on its original A4 letterhead.

What gets printed

HeaderThe clinic's own letterhead, untouched
PatientName, age/sex, mobile, date, unique Rx number
MedicinesNumbered table with form, strength, dose, timing, duration and notes. Text shrinks to fit the mapped box.
AdviceInvestigations, advice, follow-up
DoctorSignature, stamp, name, qualification, registration number and council
FileRX_261116_0001_Rahul_Verma.pdf, exact page size of the template (A4, A5, Letter…)

Checked before handover

60/60 mock tests

On both the online and the offline build: login, uploads, the 10-template limit, field editor, doctors, medicines, validation, rendering accuracy, 30-prescription bulk run, no-patient-data storage, sharing, security (XSS, CSV injection, bad backups), phone layout.

16/16 smoke checks

The full flow end to end in both builds. The offline file made zero network requests.

Fixed in this round

  • Phone: the getting-started shortcuts and "Forgot password?" were too small to tap (15–19 px); now 40 px.
  • Sample letterheads: the stamp printed over the follow-up line; layouts corrected.

Limits to know

  • Tested in Chrome/Chromium; check Safari and real phones yourself.
  • The login protects the screen, not the data: anyone with the laptop and browser profile can reach it.
  • PDFs are image-based (text isn't selectable).
